_comment: List-valued parts of the fact-checking prompt. Each list becomes a CheckboxGroup in the UI (all items selected by default) and is rendered into prompts/sections/*.md via Jinja2. Items are copied verbatim from prompts/original_prompt.md, except two corrected spellings (Terence Tao, John von Neumann; see tests/test_prompts.py SPELLING); claim_types extends the user's list from the feature request.
verdict_labels: doing logical fallacies and which ones
result of cognitive biases and which ones
not taking other valid perspectives (assumptions, definitions, models, measurements, conclusions, etc.) into account
mistaking philosophical assumption for empirical fact
_conditions_comment: Evaluative conditions of the original prompt that get their own per-claim finding, score_pct and confidence_pct in the JSON summary. Each is enabled only while its section is selected (Lego-style); score defines what 0-100% means.

conditions.name: omitted nuance, context and complexity
conditions.score: how much important nuance, context and complexity the claim omits (0 = nothing important omitted)

conditions.name: empiricist perspective
conditions.score: how well the claim holds up given the empirical evidence

conditions.name: rationalist perspective
conditions.score: how well the claim holds up under logical, a priori analysis

conditions.name: Bayesian perspective
conditions.score: subjective Bayesian-style assessment of support under stated priors and evidence; not a computed or calibrated posterior probability

conditions.name: frequentist perspective
conditions.score: how well the claim is supported by frequentist evidence (significance, effect sizes, replication, error rates)

conditions.name: predictive power
conditions.score: how many precise, testable predictions the claim makes

conditions.name: explanatory power
conditions.score: how much the claim explains, compressed into how few assumptions
